name: Indirect operating cash flow
objective: Explain and apply indirect operating cash flow.
explanation: The indirect method reconciles net income to operating cash flow by adjusting for noncash expenses, nonoperating items and operating working-capital changes. An increase in receivables consumes cash relative to accrual revenue.
why: Add back noncash depreciation and subtract the uncollected receivable increase: 50 + 10 − 8 = 52.
definition: The indirect method reconciles net income to operating cash flow by adjusting for noncash expenses, nonoperating items and operating working-capital changes.
example: Net income 50 + depreciation 10 − receivables increase 8 = CFO 52, with no other adjustments.
trap: Increasing operating liabilities generally adds cash; increasing operating assets generally uses cash.
mnemonic: Indirect operating cash flow → Increasing operating liabilities generally adds cash; increasing operating assets generally uses cash.
recall: Without looking: explain indirect operating cash flow and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: The indirect method reconciles net income to operating cash flow by adjusting for noncash expenses, nonoperating items and operating working-capital changes. An increase in receivables consumes cash relative to accrual revenue. Watch for: Increasing operating liabilities generally adds cash; increasing operating assets generally uses cash.

name: Free cash flow to the firm
objective: Explain and apply free cash flow to the firm.
explanation: FCFF is cash available to both debt and equity providers after operating needs and capital investment. Starting from CFO, add after-tax interest when interest was deducted in CFO, then subtract capital expenditure.
why: Restore the after-tax interest cash flow to all providers: 90 + 10(1 − .30) − 40 = 57.
definition: FCFF is cash available to both debt and equity providers after operating needs and capital investment.
example: CFO 90, interest paid and included in CFO 10, tax rate 30%, capex 40: FCFF = 90 + 7 − 40 = 57.
trap: The CFO-based formula depends on where interest is classified.
mnemonic: Free cash flow to the firm → The CFO-based formula depends on where interest is classified.
recall: Without looking: explain free cash flow to the firm and one mistake to avoid.
recallAnswer: FCFF is cash available to both debt and equity providers after operating needs and capital investment. Starting from CFO, add after-tax interest when interest was deducted in CFO, then subtract capital expenditure. Watch for: The CFO-based formula depends on where interest is classified.

formula.name: Three-part DuPont ROE
formula.expression: ROE = (NI / Sales) × (Sales / Avg assets) × (Avg assets / Avg equity)
formula.variables: NI: net income; use consistent average balance-sheet quantities
formula.intuition: Diagnose whether profitability, efficiency or leverage drives ROE.
formula.when: Diagnose whether profitability, efficiency or leverage drives ROE.
formula.mistake: Do not interpret leverage-driven ROE as pure operating improvement.
